content.comment_body: Hello, I'm considering purchasing [product_name] and am unsure which version would be suitable. My application involves temperature measurement and heater control, with both automatic and manual modes. Is it possible to use [product_name] [version_no] software together with [product_name] [version_no] and the [product_name] controller [article_no]? I'm specifically interested in connecting to the device via a browser on the local network. I've read that there have been issues with newer versions of [product_name] [version_no], so before making a purchase, I want to be sure the connection will function reliably. Thank you in advance.

[product_name] [version_no] typically works well within a local network environment. Issues mainly arise when publishing content externally, for example to AWS. If you are only accessing the web page from your device within the local network, then [product_name] [version_no] should be suitable. You will need to insert a microSD card into the slot on the device to upload a webpage from [product_name] [version_no]. Be sure to follow the proper steps to format the card before use.

Keep in mind the SD card capacity should not exceed 32 GB. If using a larger card, create a partition no larger than 32 GB and format it with FAT32. I operate a [product_name] [version_no] ([article_no]) on a local network and use its extended web server. However, browser compatibility can impact performance, so certain browsers may experience issues.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are seeking detailed information about compatibility and access between different versions of [product_name] software and hardware, as well as network connectivity and browser support. Concerns include local network accessibility, requirements for microSD card usage, issues reported for specific software versions, and potential problems with certain browsers. The general consensus is that the setup works locally with proper hardware and formatting but may have browser-dependent limitations.
